profile.title: Synthetic intracellular-amount apoptosis commitment and feedback

validity.population: one synthetic cell represented by one homogeneous intracellular drug inventory
validity.physiological_state: software verification only; no physiological or disease state
validity.description: A dimensionless Hill surrogate maps final intracellular drug amount to an effect fraction; crossing a declared synthetic threshold commits the cell to an irreversible apoptosis state and emits a neutral higher-layer event.

sources.citation: Wendt, Regine (2024), Einsatz von Nanotechnologien in der Praezisionsmedizin, Sections 4.4-4.5 and 5.4
sources.role: localized drug release, cell response, apoptosis, and higher-layer scenario vision

sources.citation: MEHLISSA Next M5.6 conservative nanodevice drug delivery
sources.role: typed intracellular drug inventory, source identity, and observation time

sources.citation: MEHLISSA Next ADR-0040 synthetic apoptosis commitment and higher-layer feedback
sources.role: dose-response surrogate, irreversible state transition, and feedback boundary

limitations: Drug, cell, half-maximal amount, Hill coefficient, threshold, and target scenario are synthetic software-test values.
The response uses final intracellular amount rather than concentration, exposure history, target binding, metabolism, or pathway dynamics.
Apoptosis commitment is an abstract irreversible state label; morphology, caspase signaling, execution time, clearance, and neighboring-tissue effects are not modeled.
The event timestamp is the model observation time and not an inferred biological commitment time.
The reference verifies arithmetic, identity, gating, and boundary semantics; it makes no efficacy, toxicity, dose, safety, treatment, or clinical claim.
